news.title: Fifa sparks tension with demand for tax-free status in UK for Women’s World Cup
news.lede: It also wants exchange-rate fees exemption for 2035. Fifa at loggerheads with UK’s four FAs and government. Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup. The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.

news.title: Junior All Whites out to impress at U-17 World Cup despite tough draw
news.lede: The last age group tournament of the year for New Zealand kicks off over the next two weeks, with the Junior All Whites ready to contest the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar. Like the women’s U-17 event, this tournament is now held annually with a host holding it every year for five years. All matches except the final will be played at the Aspire Zone, a large multi-pitch facility in Doha, while the final will be held at the nearby 45,000-capacity Ahmad bin Ali Stadium. Forty-eight teams will take part, including eight tournament debutants.

news.title: France's Diallo, Japan's Tashima challenging Infantino in FIFA election
news.lede: GENEVA — FIFA president Gianni Infantino is officially facing two election opponents who are trying to end his 11 years in office following his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan met the midnight deadline overnight in Zurich to file entry papers with nomination letters from five member federations, FIFA confirmed on Thursday. Later Thursday, Infantino and Tashima sat near each other in a Bangkok theater at the annual awards gala for the Asian Football Confederation, separated by one row and a few seats. The vote by FIFA's 211 member federations, 46 of them in Asia, is on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco.

news.title: Women’s World Cup play-offs: How they work
news.lede: England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are preparing for play-off finals in December as they try to qualify for the 2027 World Cup. But how do they work and what are the Inter-Confederations play-offs? Match of the Day Wales presenter Catrin Heledd breaks things down.
